mbm-0776.clue: My computer knows when I’ve forgotten the fern.
mbm-0776.quote: I drew a pixel fern that droops on Thursdays, our watering day. The real one is enormous now. I’ve had to teach the little one in the computer to grow a second frond.

mbm-0777.clue: I asked my brothers for their worst ties.
mbm-0777.quote: I unpicked every loud necktie in the house for a quilt of stained-glass fish. The one with the yellow bubbles used to attend weddings around Dad’s neck.

mbm-0778.clue: I can reach my favorite hold with my eyes shut.
mbm-0778.quote: There’s a stone shaped like a thumbprint halfway up the climbing wall. I used to stop there to worry. These days I stop and watch my best friend make the same move below me.

mbm-0779.clue: I paddle with a tiny passenger.
mbm-0779.quote: At the gentle end of our rafting trip, a green frog landed on my paddle blade. I held it flat like a waiter carrying soup until we reached the bank.

mbm-0780.clue: I keep one collar in my coat pocket.
mbm-0780.quote: My lifting coach painted a daisy on the clamp for my weight bar. I can spot my station from across the room. She adds another petal when I learn a new lift.

mbm-0781.quote: I was juggling three clementines when one burst against the kitchen ceiling. I switched to beanbags indoors. The little orange stain still gets a laugh from my upstairs neighbor.

mbm-0782.clue: I can play a sunrise on the keyboard.
mbm-0782.quote: I wrote a program that turns notes from my keyboard into stripes of color on the monitor. My mother played her breakfast song and got a perfectly pink sunrise.

mbm-0783.clue: I made a blanket out of missed trains.
mbm-0783.quote: Every time I missed my stop after a night game, I saved a ticket. I copied the colored stripes in cloth. My couch quilt goes farther north than I ever meant to.

mbm-0784.clue: I brought a brush for a golf ball.
mbm-0784.quote: A muddy ball came up with a perfect leaf shape pressed into it. I sat beside the green and painted it in my notebook before I wiped the ball clean.

mbm-0785.clue: I have a map you can sleep under.
mbm-0785.quote: Our quilt follows the creek behind my cousins’ houses. I used wavy blue stitching for the water and put one crooked picnic bench right where ours sank into the mud.

mbm-0786.quote: Grandma stitched three corners of my first quilt. At the fourth she slid the needle over to me. Now my nephew is learning, and that corner has been waiting for him.

mbm-0787.clue: I’ve got an audience at my kitchen sink.
mbm-0787.quote: I hung a hummingbird feeder where I wash dishes. One morning a green visitor hovered beside the soap bubbles. I let the breakfast plates soak another minute.

mbm-0788.clue: I own half a pencil and a whole trophy.
mbm-0788.quote: My niece used our score pencil as a miniature flagpole. I sank the putt beside it. She stuck the pencil in a lump of clay and presented it to me at dinner.

mbm-0789.clue: I pack a pillowcase with a hole in it.
mbm-0789.quote: We held a sock-puppet show inside our tent when the rain came. My pillowcase moon rose through a gap in the blanket curtain. The people in the next tent applauded.

mbm-0790.clue: I keep a pebble in my chalk bag.
mbm-0790.quote: My daughter tried a tiny climbing wall while I tried the big one. We met on the ground and traded summit rocks. Hers fits perfectly beside my chalk.

mbm-0791.clue: I learned the fast part in a kitchen.
mbm-0791.quote: I tapped the tricky choro rhythm along with my aunt chopping onions. At the next music circle my fingers finally kept up with the guitar, and all I could think about was supper.

mbm-0792.clue: One of my robots walks with a limp.
mbm-0792.quote: I built a model with one short leg, so my sister cut a tiny platform shoe from a pink eraser. It’s the flashiest robot on my shelf. I gave it a matching shield.

mbm-0793.clue: I owe the audience a third scarf.
mbm-0793.quote: My juggling act ended with two scarves in my hands and one floating from the ceiling lamp. We opened the windows and had tea beneath the world’s slowest encore.

mbm-0794.clue: I keep all the little moons.
mbm-0794.quote: After cutting circles for my quilt, I had a basket of fabric crescents. I stitched them into a night sky for the back. Everybody turns the blanket over first.

mbm-0795.clue: I can bring home an echo.
mbm-0795.quote: I kayaked beneath a stone bridge singing one note. My friend answered from the far side and the bridge sang a third one. Now we slow down there every trip.

mbm-0796.clue: I saved the red ski for the photo.
mbm-0796.quote: After months on two water skis, I finally dropped one and stayed upright. On the dock I propped the spare against my shoulder like a teammate who deserved a picture too.

mbm-0797.quote: My first mittens came out different sizes. I gave the big one to Dad and the small one to my little cousin. They held up their mitten hands together for a surprisingly good portrait.

mbm-0798.clue: I can hear the tune before the door opens.
mbm-0798.quote: Our bassist knocks the rhythm of our favorite son on the porch rail. I answer with my claves from inside. Last week we finished a whole verse before anybody let him in.

mbm-0799.clue: I keep paper boats in my books.
mbm-0799.quote: I fold my bookmarks into little sailboats. When I finish a good adventure I float its boat in the washbasin. My sister watches the fleet and picks her next read.

mbm-0800.clue: I can juggle breakfast without cracking it.
mbm-0800.quote: My brother mistook my painted wooden eggs for groceries. When I tossed all three, he dived under the table with a mixing bowl. We’ve added him to the act.
